title: Term Length Limits for Domain Registrations
content:
# Term Length Limits for Domain Registrations

Registry rule sheet for Domain Registrations: the number of whole years a registration, renewal, transfer or restore covers, and the furthest an expiry date may lie in the future.

| TLD product | Minimum years per new registration | Maximum years an expiry date may lie beyond the current date | Minimum years per renewal order | Years added by a completed inbound transfer | Renewal years included in a restore |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .us Domain Registration | 1 | 10 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| .ca Domain Registration | 1 | 10 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| .com Domain Registration | 1 | 10 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| .org Domain Registration | 1 | 10 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| .net Domain Registration | 1 | 10 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| .co Domain Registration | 1 | 10 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| .io Domain Registration | 1 | 10 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

## Basis notes

- The maximum applies after any registration, renewal, transfer or restore: the resulting expiry date may lie no more than 10 years after the current date on every TLD product of Domain Registrations.
- A new registration and a renewal order each cover at least 1 whole year.
- A completed inbound transfer adds 1 year to the expiry date the domain carried at the registry.
- A redemption restore is charged together with 1 renewal year, which it adds to the expiry date.

## Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical .org Domain Registration that is renewed on a day when its expiry date lies 3 years and 2 months ahead can have its expiry date moved at most to a date 10 years after that day; a renewal order for it still covers at least 1 whole year.
